uncited: This family defines methods for representing volume data using a recursive subdivision of 3D space into octants, enabling adaptive resolution where detail is concentrated in regions of interest.
It solves the problem of efficiently storing and rendering complex, multi-scale volumetric data that would be prohibitive to store on a uniform grid.

Unlike [Homogeneity-Based KD-Tree Construction](1325-homogeneity-based-kd-tree-construction.md) which uses axis-aligned splits based on data homogeneity, or [TET-AMR Data Structure](1094-tet-amr-data-structure.md) which uses unstructured tetrahedra, octree methods maintain a regular hierarchical topology that simplifies traversal and ray intersection logic.
